# sandcastle-kit

> An opinionated issue-burndown kit built on Sandcastle by Matt Pocock. It runs Claude Code agents unattended in Docker sandboxes, one per ticket: an implement agent, a stronger review agent, the project's own gates run by the orchestrator, green branches merged locally, nothing pushed. Tickets are GitHub Issues or Markdown files in the repo. Each ticket lands as it goes green, a conflict gets one more try in the same run, and a ticket whose blocker lands starts at once. Sandboxes are lean: the project's skills and MCP servers are hidden from agents unless kept, and its plugins always. An agent skill (/sandcastle in Claude Code, $sandcastle in Codex, read by OpenCode) sets a project up, audits a repo for work and files it as tickets, triages tickets into the queue, starts and closes runs, and updates the kit. First-class support for Herdr (https://herdr.dev): a plugin that opens the status view over any tab, and the run's progress in Herdr's sidebar. An optional Claude Code mod shows a run above the prompt of the session where /sandcastle was used, tells that session when the run ends, and between runs shows how many tickets are ready in its status line. macOS and Linux. MIT licence.

An AI coding agent setting this up for someone should start at the README's section written for agents, then run `sandcastle doctor`.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/henkisdabro/sandcastle-kit/blob/main/README.md): who it is for, quick start, how a run works, configuration, safety model, troubleshooting
- [For AI coding agents](https://github.com/henkisdabro/sandcastle-kit/blob/main/README.md#-if-you-are-an-ai-coding-agent-reading-this): the steps an agent follows to install and use the kit
- [Install](https://github.com/henkisdabro/sandcastle-kit/blob/main/docs/INSTALL.md): requirements, what `sandcastle setup` does, a manual install, updating
- [Changelog](https://github.com/henkisdabro/sandcastle-kit/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md): releases, with Upgrading notes per version
